2 FY27 Earnings Call. 
 
Joining me today are Mr. Niraj Kaushik, Deputy CEO, Mr. Gaurav Seth, Chief Financial Officer, 
and Mr. Sovan Satyaprakash, Chief Strategy and Investor Relations Officer. Also joining us is 
our Investor Relations Advisors from Strategic Growth Advisors. Our financial results, investor 
presentation, and press release are all available on the stock exchanges as well as on the website 
for your guidance. 
 
Aye Finance continues to make a solid headway towards our mission to provide inclusive formal 
credit to micro-entrepreneurs across India, and with 6.9 lakh active borrowers, which span over 
18 states and three union territories. Lending to Indian micro and MSME segment continues to 
remain a significantly underpenetrated area, and this offers a substantial long-term structural 
opportunity to us.  
 
We occupy a dominant position in this market and have a deep understanding of this segment. 
Our differentiated approach, which combines proprietary underwriting models, physical branch 
origination, enhanced with AI and machine learning, uniquely position us to capture this market 
responsibly. 
 
To summarize Q2 FY27, this was a quarter of steady and encouraging progress. Year-on-year, 
the AUM grew by 26%. The credit cost decreased to 3.82%, improving for the seventh 
consecutive quarter, and it now lies within our guided range.  
 
The operating expense ratio also declined to 8.6%, roughly a 32 basis points improvement over 
last quarter, and all this resulted in profit after tax more than doubling. So, this solid first half 
has significantly enhanced our conviction to deliver on our stated FY27 guidance.

Now, let me briefly touch upon the operating environment before I get into the quarterly 
performance in a little more detail. The grassroot micro-MSME segment in India is showing a 
steady momentum supported by government initiatives for increasing formalization, and we 
continue to see this constructive demand in our markets for working capital across our core 
segments. 
 
The year FY27 has started on a good note as reflected in the robust trends in our business metrics. 
Our performance in Q1, which is typically a slower quarter, was rather robust, and the quarter 2 
performance has continued to build the positive trajectory, and we are today trending happily 
towards our guidance target for the year on all the salient metrics. 
 
The possibility of inflation or El Niño effects or rainfall have not materially impacted our 
customer segment and their trade demand. I had highlighted in my last quarter call the IMD 
forecast of below normal rainfall in Central India and Southern peninsula. Droughts have finally 
been declared in some parts of Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh, so that's not a 
surprise. 
 
Together, these states account for about 18% of our AUM, and we have consciously slowed our 
disbursements in some of these districts, as we believe that in lending discretion should be a 
better part of valor. 
 
Otherwise, the lending environment remains encouraging, with resilient asset quality through 
the seasonally weaker July to September quarter. Our largest states, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and 
Rajasthan, were largely unaffected by the monsoon, as can be seen in the Slide 26  in the investor 
presentation. The credit demand held up well, and we are seeing early signs of festive pick-up 
as we move into the second half of the year. 
 
On growth, our assets under management stood at INR7,597 crores, which is up 26% year-on-
year and 4% quarter-on-quarter, keeping us within our full-year guidance of 25% to 30% growth. 
Against this backdrop, our disbursements for Q2 FY27 stood at INR1,403 crores, up 10% year-
on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter, and we added 49,000 new borrowers added in this quarter. 
 
While the fresh disbursements grew at a brisk pace, and fresh disbursements of 49,000 new 
customers translates to about 23% growth in our disbursements year-on-year and 11% growth 
quarter-on-quarter, it is our repeat loans where we saw some deferment of loans, and I think it's 
primarily because the festive season has shifted into the third quarter. 
 
In repeat loans, we saw, against the year-on-year, a 3% lesser disbursement, and against quarter-
on-quarter, we were plus 10% of disbursements. Repeat is an area where I think we will make 
up because the customer ultimately needs money before the festive season, so we should see a 
better quarter in quarter 3. 
 
This took our first half FY27 disbursements to 2,622 crores, which is 15% up year-on-year. 
Historically, the first half year typically accounts for around 40% of our annual disbursements. 
The approaching festive season typically provides a lift in disbursements in the second half of 
the year, so we are well-positioned to benefit from this seasonality.

We ended quarter 2 without adding to our tally of 571 branches, which we started with the year, 
but in quarter 3, 30-plus new branches will also become operational, and this will further add 
fillip to our disbursements, and this is as per plan. 
 
Looking at efficiency and portfolio quality, driving efficiency by reducing unit costs and 
improving the asset quality remain the two key priorities for FY27. I had said that in my earlier 
investor call, and I repeat that again. 
 
And you can see demonstrated performance against these two parameters. First of all, our AUM 
per employee increased to 0.67 crores in quarter 2 as compared to 0.57 crores in the 
corresponding quarter of last year, which is an improvement of almost 18%. The AUM per 
branch also improved to 13.3 crores in quarter 2 versus 12.8 crores in quarter 1. 
 
The operating expense ratio, which fell down to 8.61% in quarter 2 versus 8.93% in quarter 1, 
so in a single quarter, we have seen a 32 basis points reduction in operating expense ratio. This 
is the reason our cost-to-income has reduced to 49%. All these summarize our efforts to make 
better use of our existing operational infrastructure and drive greater efficiency as we scale the 
business, and we see further rooms for improvement in the remaining year to come. 
 
Turning to asset quality, portfolio performance continued to improve during the quarter. Our 
GNPA has now declined for seven consecutive quarters and stood at 4.20% as of September 
2026. This is 30 basis points lower than the last quarter and 70 basis points lower year-on-year. 
 
PAR X stood at 6.94%, which is down 7 basis points sequentially and 109 points year-on-year 
from the 8.03% in Q2 FY26. These trends reflect the progress we have made in strengthening 
our portfolio quality. We target to get the PAR X to move gradually to a range below 6.5% by 
the end of the year. 
 
The vintage of our portfolio provides further comfort. As of September 2026, 95% of our current 
book was originated after June 2024. So, this is a book that has been originated after the volatile 
period of industry-wide overlending. 
 
On the credit costs, our credit costs for the quarter came in at 3.82%, which is an 21 basis points 
improvement from 4.03% in quarter 1, and 119 basis points year-on-year. We are now within 
our FY27 guided range for credit costs where we had guided for 3.5% to 4%. 
 
This reduction in credit costs was driven by 3 factors, tighter underwriting, stronger collections, 
and better repayment behavior of our customers as their business cash flows improved. We 
expect credit costs for the full year to remain within our guided range. Collections remained 
healthy, with overall non-OD collection efficiency at 99.2% and Bucket 1 collection efficiency 
at 52.8%. 
 
As mentioned earlier, these are very good collection efficiencies, and the large states of Bihar, 
Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan, which account for a significant share of our portfolio, continue to 
deliver very good collection efficiencies, which is shown in our investor presentation.

Looking at balance sheet and debt funding, our balance sheet is ready for growth. With a capital 
adequacy of 41%, as we mentioned last quarter, our current capital is sufficient to support our 
growth for around the next 2 years without needing fresh equity. 
 
Funding cost also continued to ease, and our incremental cost of borrowing declined to 10.04% 
in quarter 2 against the 10.20% in quarter 1. And this decline seems to be against the grain of 
increasing interest rates, but this is driven by an improved funding mix and our recent rating 
upgrade to IND A+. 
 
The overall blended cost of borrowing also, not only the incremental cost, but blended cost 
overall has declined 15 basis points to 10.63% in Q2 FY27 as compared to 10.78% in quarter 1. 
As older, higher-cost borrowings are repaid, we expect this benefit to flow through progressively 
over the coming quarters. 
 
Our financial performance also strengthened during the quarter. And let's talk of profits and 
margins. Gross total income for Q2 FY27 was INR527 crores compared to INR427 crores in Q2 
FY26, an increase of 23% year-on-year and 8% quarter-on-quarter. Net interest margin was 
15.6%, comfortably above our full-year guidance of 14.25% to 14.75%. 
 
A lot of people might think that there's a gap between what we are actually seeing in net interest 
margin and our guidance. The primary reason is that our guidance had factored in more 
aggressive increase in repo rates. Also, we had not factored in the rating upgrade, which we were 
expecting, but we thought it prudent not to factor it into our forecast. 
 
Pre-provision operating profit grew to a 54% year-on-year and 11% quarter-on-quarter to 
INR198 crores. This translated into stronger profitability, with profit after tax of INR87 crores, 
which is up 151% year-on-year and up 16% quarter-on-quarter. 
 
On costs, our operating expense ratio for Q2 was 8.6% compared to 8.9% in Q1, which I 
mentioned before. These improvements have resulted in the ROA, and return on total assets, 
improving to 4% in quarter 2 compared to 3.7% in quarter 1. 
 
For the first half of FY27, gross total income was INR1,017 crores, up 23% year-on-year, with 
net interest margin of 15.9%. Pre-provision operating profit also grew 47% year-on-year to 
INR377 crores. And profit after tax rose to INR162 crores from INR65 crores compared to the 
first half of FY26, which is an increase of 148%. 
 
Return on asset and return on equity for first half FY27 stood at 3.89% and 12.32%, respectively. 
At the half-way mark, we are on track to deliver on each of the salient metrics of our annual 
guidance. At the start of the year, we guided for AUM growth of 25% to 30%, credit cost of 
3.5% to 4%, net interest margin of 14.25% to 14.75%, and operating expenses of 8.25% to 
8.75%, yielding a return on asset of 4% to 4.5%, and these are return on total assets. 
 
AUM growth and credit costs are already within our guided range, and NIM continues to run 
comfortably ahead of our guidance. As volumes build in the second half, we expect the operating 
expenses and the return on asset to move into their guided ranges in line with the seasonal 
patterns of our business.

As we enter the seasonally stronger second half, our aim remains to build on this momentum 
while remaining mindful of our operating environment. The rising interest rate environment is 
already factored into our NIM guidance, as I mentioned. We are mindful of the prospective 
insurance commission recommendations, and we shall work on levers to compensate for this 
impact. 
 
And the levers are going to be, reduction in operating expense ratio, which will continue, the 
benefit that we are getting from reduction in the blended cost of borrowing, and the falling credit 
costs. We will continue to pursue our growth plans, strengthen our collection, and improve 
operational efficiency, and maintain discipline and underwriting standards. 
 
What is the vision beyond? Beyond this year, our focus remains on building a stronger and more 
sustainable lending franchise in line with the 3-year vision that we had shared in July, which 
essentially targets 28% to 33% AUM growth CAGR, return on assets of 4% to 4.5%, and as part 
of this, we are also evaluating gold loans and other secured products for our customers and will 
update you on these plans as they take shape. 
 
Our approach on these is to create a basket which addresses all the needs of our target segment, 
which is micro-enterprise borrowers, and I think we hope to see this take shape later in the year. 
 
With that, I would like to conclude my opening remarks and open the floor to questions.
